solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Large amounts of corporal punishment!

definitions.meaning: plenty, heaps, loads of something, as in a dish with generous helpings of cream
beatings with a whip or cane, a series of strokes delivered as a penalty

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how much caning went on, perhaps at an old-fashioned school.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'of' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is informal British for plenty, and also the plural of a whipping stroke, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Capital was used up supporting conflict

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the one it holds up, so it comes second

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word was is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Something that was consumed while an army fought on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used up' signals a reversal because in a down clue the letters read upwards; 'supporting' puts that piece beneath the conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

clue.text: Intrude in health resort, breaking lock?

indicators.note: the resort word breaks into the lock word, splitting it open around itself

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A burglar forcing a lock to get into a spa hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' looks like a door fitting but means a lock of hair; 'breaking' puts the resort inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to go onto someone's property or space without right, which is the legal wrong of entering unlawfully.

clue.text: Couple I encountered going north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a pair they bumped into while travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' reverses only 'encountered' in this down clue, which then follows I.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantically linked pair is informally called an item.

clue.text: Female ruler, a raider from Scandinavia

parts.note: Vi is a woman's name, short for Violet, so it stands for a female
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A female monarch who was also a Norse raider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' gives a girl's name, VI, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse seafarers who raided Europe from Scandinavia in the early Middle Ages are known by this name.

clue.text: Give up bird food, so to speak

indicators.note: the phrase signals that we want a word as spoken, matching another in sound

parts.note: seed is what birds are fed

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning feeding the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' tells us SEED is said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender or yield something, especially territory, is to cede it.

clue.text: Priest heading off beast of burden

indicators.note: the first letter, the head of the word, is taken off

parts.note: a llama is a South American pack animal

explanation.surface: A cleric setting off on a pack animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like departing but removes the first letter of LLAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Buddhist spiritual teacher in Tibet is called by this title, a kind of monk or priest.

clue.text: Old family servant's fee for continued employment

definitions.meaning: a long-serving domestic servant kept on by a household
a fee paid in advance to secure the services of a lawyer or adviser

explanation.surface: What a loyal butler is paid to stay on.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'servant' stands for 'is', linking the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a servant retained by a family and a fee paid to keep a professional on call.

clue.text: Dissertation provided by one of the siblings?

parts.note: sis is short for sister, one among the siblings

explanation.surface: An academic paper written by one of a family's children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of the siblings' reads as THE plus SIS, a sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A long essay presenting original research for a degree is a dissertation or thesis.

clue.text: For a young girl it's sort of over

definitions.meaning: an unmarried young woman, a lass
in cricket an over is a set of six balls; one with no runs scored has a special name

explanation.surface: Something said to be suitable for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket over is six balls bowled by one bowler; one in which no runs are scored is a maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an unmarried girl and also a scoreless over in cricket.

clue.text: Precipitation beginning to settle at the present time

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word means its first letter

parts.note: now means at the present time

explanation.surface: Rain or sleet starting to lie on the ground at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is frozen water falling from clouds, one form of precipitation.

clue.text: Completely grisly setting for end of detective story?

indicators.note: the two words around it act as a setting, holding the jewel-like letter inside

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone
gory means grisly, bloody

indicators.note: the end of the word means its last letter

explanation.surface: A gruesome finale to a murder mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting for' puts E, the last letter of 'detective', inside the phrase for 'Completely grisly'; the question mark flags the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a tale whose characters and events carry a hidden moral meaning, so it is a kind of story; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Academic visiting recluse, a capital person

indicators.note: a visitor goes into someone's place, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a loner keeps to themself, like a recluse
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A university lecturer calling on a hermit who is a fine fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like 'excellent' but refers to a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from England's capital city is called a Londoner.

clue.text: One climbing quickly — not the winner, though

definitions.meaning: someone who sprints up a hill or stairs, a runner going up

explanation.surface: A fast climber who still did not take first place.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is read literally: a runner going up. 'though' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor who finishes in second place is the runner-up; read literally, a runner going upwards.

clue.text: One who kills a couple of idiots at home

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the word for a fool appears twice

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot
in means at home

explanation.surface: A murderer is a pair of fools staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer, especially of a prominent figure.

clue.text: A second-class thoroughfare overseas

parts.note: B is the grade below A, second class
a road is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A minor road in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a B-road is a secondary road, below an A-road.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means in or to a foreign country, overseas.

clue.text: In Bhagalpur, an incomparable queen

indicators.note: the letters sit in the clue text, concealed across the words

explanation.surface: An unrivalled queen in the Indian city of Bhagalpur.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of Bhagalpur, 'an' and the start of 'incomparable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is the wife of a rajah or an Indian queen in her own right.

clue.text: Reject rubbish

definitions.meaning: to turn down or decline, a verb

explanation.walkthrough: Stress changes the word: re-FUSE as a verb, REF-use as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means decline; as a noun it is household waste.

clue.text: Pub dispute in Cumbrian town

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A fight in a pub in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow-in-Furness is a town in Cumbria, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow, short for Barrow-in-Furness, is a shipbuilding town in that county.

clue.text: Girl accepting ring in the near future

indicators.note: the girl takes in the ring, holding it inside her name

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
O is round, like a ring

explanation.surface: A girl accepting a ring, so a wedding soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word meaning soon, shortly.

clue.text: Farm vehicle fashionable south of Washington

indicators.note: in a down clue being south means lying below, so this piece comes second

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for Washington state
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy tractor parked south of the US capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A wain is an old word for a farm wagon, as in Constable's painting The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Compensate for position of unemployed film actor

definitions.meaning: to counterbalance or make up for, a verb
an actor not working is away from the filming location, read as two words

explanation.surface: Making up for being a film actor out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is read as two words: off, not on, the set.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a loss is to counterbalance it; an idle actor is literally off the set.

clue.text: What Casanova would do, informed about eastern state

indicators.note: the outer word goes about, around, the other one

parts.note: wise means informed or knowing
Oman is a state in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Something a famous seducer might do, told about a country in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Casanova was an 18th-century Venetian famous for his many love affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue many casual affairs with women is to womanise, Casanova's famous habit.

clue.text: Sound of only form of Black American music?

indicators.note: we want a word said aloud that matches another word in sound

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: Asking whether a style of music is the only one of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul is a genre of popular music rooted in African-American gospel and rhythm and blues.
